raw_case_text:
A 29-year-old male was referred to our hospital due to general weakness for the last 7 months, abdominal discomfort, intermittent fever, and pancytopenia. According to his anamnesis, he was previously a healthy person without any serious illnesses. He was a computer technician and a tourist guide. He was suspected to have a blood malignancy by the previous referrer hospital due to repeated infections. He presented with several large ecchymoses in his lower extremities and trunk (Figure 5). An abdominal palpation revealed an enlarged liver measuring 3 cm below the costal margin and splenomegaly with Schuffner grade 2. The laboratory results revealed pancytopenia with a hemoglobin level of 6.2 g/dl, a leukocyte count of 1 x 103/mul, a neutrophil count of 0.69 x 103/mul, and a platelet count of 21 x 103/mul. Procalcitonin was 2.11 ng/ml, SGOT 107 U/L, SGPT 33 U/L, total bilirubin 4.96 mg/dl with direct bilirubin 4.8 mg/dl. There was a disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) as indicated with fibrinogen 0.35 g/L, APTT > 400 sec, PPT > 320 sec, and D-Dimer 572 ng/mL. The serology of HIV, hepatitis B and C, and ANA IF were negative. The thorax X-ray showed bronchitis.
The BMA smear showed hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) with abundant H. capsulatum inside the macrophage cells with dyserythropoiesis and dysgranulopoiesis (Figure 6). Sabouraud agar was used to grow some of the BMA samples. The isolate was subsequently taken after 5 weeks and stained with methylene blue and KOH (Figure 7). A sensitivity test showed good response to several antifungals, such as voriconazole, fluconazole, ketoconazole, and miconazole. The patient was managed with voriconazole 200 mg intravenously every 12 hours for 3 days, followed by itraconazole 3 x 200 mg in the first 3 days, followed by 2 x 200 mg planned for 3 months. Other therapies included intravenous antibiotics, G-CSF injection, supportive transfusion of packed red cells, platelets, fresh frozen plasma, and albumin infusion. We observed gradual improvement in clinical and laboratory parameters during hospitalization, and the patient was discharged after 30 days. The blood evaluation during treatment is shown in Figure 8. One week after discharge, a blood evaluation showed improvement in hemoglobin level of 8.5 g/dl, leukocyte count of 2.9 x 103/mul, neutrophil count of 2.1 x 103/mul, and platelet of count 109 x 103/mul.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 29-year-old male presented with a 7-month history of generalized weakness, abdominal discomfort, intermittent fever, and pancytopenia, accompanied by large cutaneous ecchymoses.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Previously healthy 29-year-old male computer technician and tour guide developed 7 months of general weakness, abdominal discomfort, recurrent infections, intermittent fever, pancytopenia, and large ecchymoses over his trunk and lower extremities, prompting referral for suspected hematologic malignancy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy without serious medical illness. Occupational history: Computer technician and tourist guide.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for generalized weakness, abdominal discomfort, intermittent fever, and truncal/lower extremity bruising.

objective.physical_examination: Skin: multiple large ecchymoses over the lower extremities and trunk. Abdomen: hepatomegaly (3 cm below the costal margin) and splenomegaly (Schuffner grade 2).
objective.routine_investigations: Labs: severe pancytopenia with Hb 6.2 g/dL, WBC 1.0 x 10^3/uL (ANC 0.69 x 10^3/uL), and platelets 21 x 10^3/uL; procalcitonin 2.11 ng/mL, AST (SGOT) 107 U/L, ALT (SGPT) 33 U/L, total bilirubin 4.96 mg/dL (direct bilirubin 4.8 mg/dL); DIC profile showing fibrinogen 0.35 g/L, aPTT >400 s, PT >320 s, and D-dimer 572 ng/mL. Negative HIV, HBV, HCV, and ANA IF serologies. Thorax X-ray: bronchitis.
objective.advanced_workup: Bone marrow aspiration (BMA) smear & Sabouraud agar culture: hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), dyserythropoiesis, dysgranulopoiesis, and abundant intracellular Histoplasma capsulatum within macrophages; Sabouraud agar culture grew H. capsulatum after 5 weeks (confirmed on methylene blue and KOH mount, with susceptibility to voriconazole, fluconazole, ketoconazole, and miconazole).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis complicated by secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) in an immunocompetent tour guide. Confirmation: Bone marrow aspirate smear showing abundant intrahistiocytic Histoplasma capsulatum and hemophagocytosis, and bone marrow culture on Sabouraud agar isolating Histoplasma capsulatum at 5 weeks. Plan & clinical course: Treated with IV voriconazole (200 mg q12h for 3 days) followed by oral itraconazole (200 mg TID x 3 days, then 200 mg BID for 3 months), alongside IV antibiotics, G-CSF, PRBCs, platelets, FFP, and albumin; discharged after 30 days with improving blood counts (1-week post-discharge Hb 8.5 g/dL, WBC 2.9 x 10^3/uL, ANC 2.1 x 10^3/uL, platelets 109 x 10^3/uL).
